messages:
emily_support: Heads-up — Acme (customer) just opened a high‑severity ticket: p95/p99 generation latency spiking across us-west-2, started ~09:10 UTC after the morning infra push. They're seeing API timeouts and auth retry storms. Attaching traces in the ticket.
rajiv_eng: Which push? driver/firmware/kernel combo? Any correlation IDs we can use to pull traces?
emily_support: Deploybot posted a driver+firmware rollout at 08:55 UTC to the GPU fleet in us-west-2. Ticket shows request ids: req=acme/trace/0451d3 — I'll paste a few traces here shortly.
deploybot: rollout: gpu-driver-525.8 -> 526.1, gpu-fw 2.14.3 applied to pool-usw2-gpu-a at 2026-03-16T08:55:12Z. Canary passed earlier in ap-south.
oliver_sre: Looking at infra metrics now — p99 generation latency for /v1/generate jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s around 09:08 UTC in pool-usw2.  IO wait and disk util tick up on several nodes. Query: avg iowait by host for pool-usw2 in the last 30m -> iowait increase from 0.8% to 7-12% on affected hosts.
metricsbot: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/board/latency?p=pool-usw2&from=2026-03-16T08:30Z&to=2026-03-16T09:30Z
zhang_eng_infra: Pulling dmesg and nvme stats from host-ustg-12 now. Snippets:
```
[  568.123456] nvme0: I/O submission timeout, reset controller
[  568.124789] nvme nvme0: failed to write meta io: -5
```
nvme-cli: 500ms tail latency spikes, avg qdepth jumped. Looks like hostfs flush storms interacting with firmware update.
rajiv_eng: Can you paste the exact driver package version on the hosts? Need to confirm kernel-driver ABI mismatch possibility.
zhang_eng_infra: Driver on host-ustg-12: nvidia-driver-526.1. Kernel is 5.19.14. We did the driver package upgrade from 525.8 -> 526.1 across pool at 08:55.
sarah_support: Customer reports timeouts escalate to 5xx and then client retries cause auth rate-limit alarms. They want immediate mitigation.
oliver_sre: Mitigation options we can enact right now: 1) route Acme's traffic to a fallback pool (us-east-1) where drivers are still 525.x; 2) enable model-variant fallback (smaller KV/cache-friendly variant) for the customer; 3) temporarily increase dedicated pod count for their tenant to reduce queueing. which do we want first?
katie_prod: Customer-facing comms: tell them we're investigating, offering route to fallback region + temporary capacity. They asked for ETA — we should give a short timeline after mitigation chosen.
rajiv_eng: Short-term: enable routing fallback for Acme -> us-east-1 and switch their default model to gen-compact-1 to reduce IO pressure. Mid-term: rollback driver on the most impacted hosts or pause firmware rollout. Long-term: add preflight io-stress check to canary.
emily_support: @rajiv_eng please coordinate routing + model switch and confirm once done, I'll update the customer. @katie_prod we'll propose 30min for routing and 60–90min for full rollback if needed.
zhang_eng_infra: Started a targeted rollback on the three worst hosts (host-ustg-12, host-ustg-14, host-ustg-19) to driver 525.8 to see if IO stabilizes. Will followup with `iostat -x 1 10` output.
oliver_sre: Also recommend setting `vm.dirty_expire_centisecs` lower on affected hosts as a temporary host kernel knob to reduce flush bursts. Patch command: `sysctl -w vm.dirty_expire_centisecs=100` (orig 3000). Only as temporary emergency mitigation.
zhang_eng_infra: iostat snapshot from host-ustg-12 after rollback start:
```
Device: r/s   w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  avgrq-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0:  4.1  1.2  512.0  128.0   160.0    2.8   0.5    5.0
```
lower but still seeing short spikes from kernel flush.
metricsbot: acme tenant p99 -> downgraded from 1.8s -> 420ms after routing switch started at 09:24 UTC.
emily_support: Customer on call — they're ok with temporary region failover for now. Please confirm any billing/latency implications and note for CS.
katie_prod: We should flag this as a potential rollback-induced risk for other customers. Create a short incident ticket and notify Accounts for potential cross-region billing adjustments.
rajiv_eng: Action items: (1) complete targeted rollback on affected hosts (zhang), (2) keep routing fallback for Acme until we verify stable p99 < 300ms for 30m (oliver), (3) pause fleet firmware rollout until root cause determined (me). I'll start a bisect on which change caused the hostfs flush interaction.
sarah_support: I'll update the support ticket and escalate SLT if customer requests escalation. Thanks team.
oliver_sre: Quick note — if rollback doesn't fully resolve, we may need to throttle hostfs flush IO via cgroup io.weight adjustments for inference pods. Low risk but more invasive.
emily_support: Thanks all — updating customer: routing fallback in place, targeted rollback started, monitoring. Will follow up in 30m. :thumbsup:
rajiv_eng: I'll post a follow-up here with bisect results and recommended permanent mitigation (kernel tuning or canary io-stress). Expect preliminary root cause in ~4 hours.
zhang_eng_infra: Rolling back finished on the three hosts at 09:41 UTC. Observed immediate drop in NVMe qdepth and iowait on those hosts. Continuing to watch fleet.
metricsbot: global p99 for generate stabilized to ~260ms at 09:48 UTC. Affected pool still slightly elevated but trending down.
katie_prod: Preparing a short customer status note and internal postmortem stub. I'll own the comms draft after you post the bisect summary.
emily_support: Closing loop for now — customer accepted fallback and is monitoring. We'll keep this thread open for the bisect and postmortem notes.
